topics.label: Welcome and Course Introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing for the lecture series, introducing the teaching team, student cohorts, and overarching learning outcomes.

topics.label: Biological Foundations: Mutation, Differentiation, and Tissue Architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how cancer develops through the stepwise accumulation of genetic and epigenetic alterations and the failure of normal cellular differentiation and three-dimensional tissue architecture.

topics.label: Tumor Invasion, Metastasis, and Histological Progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the mechanisms and histological hallmarks of tumor invasion and metastasis, contrasting benign and malignant behaviors through tissue sections and the colorectal adenoma-to-carcinoma sequence.

topics.label: Tumor Classification, Nomenclature, and Mechanisms of Pathogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the naming conventions for benign and malignant neoplasms and outline the physiological mechanisms by which tumors cause organ dysfunction, clinical illness, and death.

topics.label: Cancer Epidemiology in Humans and Across Animal Taxa
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the incidence and mortality rates of major human cancer types and compare tumor prevalence across different animal species.

topics.label: Principles, Modalities, and Challenges of Cancer Screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the clinical rationale for early cancer detection and evaluate the implementation, efficacy, and limitations of screening programs across different cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Next Steps
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing framing, summarizing the session against the learning outcomes and outlining upcoming practicals and lectures.
